description:
## Why
A delegator must obtain a tagged artifact without tying up Hyperion or competing with the operator for its one-build lock. The six-week 1.0 delivery clock starts when this route lands. Backlog item: F1.

## Evidence
- All c11 code citations below are on origin/main `0ff8887e5e`; upstream citations are on upstream/main `920ff39ff7`.
- c11: `scripts/reload.sh:282` builds locally and `scripts/reload.sh:302` invokes xcodebuild under the host lock; `scripts/reloads.sh:233` does the same for staging. `scripts/test-unit.sh:17` is the locked test entry point; `scripts/with-build-lock.sh:42` serializes the machine.
- Existing C11-216 description and 2026-09-12 comments record a remote-build draft and an Xcode prerequisite; these are historical observations, not current Atlas readiness proof.
- Research: BACKLOG.md F1/D26; feature-audit-fable.md §3 and §7; feature-audit-astra.md §3; c11-1.0.html §06 Six weeks. No upstream PR is required for this infrastructure task.

## Scope
In: remote tagged, test and release-build routes, artifact/log retrieval, exact source identity, cache provisioning and delegator instructions. Out: F2 fleet soak implementation, remote-agent federation/PTY holders, production publishing and unrelated CI cleanup.

## Approach
Refresh Atlas readiness before relying on the September probe. Inspect, do not assume completed, the prior `c11-216-remote-build` worktree draft (`scripts/remote-build.sh`, reloads no-launch work). Prefer a thin SSH remote entry around existing build/test scripts. Transfer the selected worktree and submodule identities into an isolated tag directory, provision SHA-keyed GhosttyKit and DerivedData, retain the one-build-per-machine lock, and return attributable artifacts and logs. Preserve the prior requirement to update c11-hotload/delegator guidance and sync installed skill copies. Signing/notarization prerequisites must be explicit; do not copy credentials into logs or the repository.

## Acceptance criteria
1. From a delegator checkout on Hyperion, request a tagged build and receive its .app, build result and source/submodule identity from Atlas; process evidence shows no Hyperion xcodebuild for that invocation.
2. Two simultaneous build requests serialize through Atlas’s host lock and keep their tag outputs separate; an Atlas build failure returns nonzero and cannot launch a stale local artifact.
3. The same remote route runs a selected test and a release build; report assertion results separately from compilation. Document and exercise the intended signing/notarization route on Atlas before claiming release-build migration complete; publishing still requires named approval.
4. Launch the returned tagged artifact using launch-tagged-automation.sh with QA startup dialogs suppressed and verify its CLI/socket identity and one terminal workflow. A delegator following the updated installed skill can repeat this without undocumented local build steps.

## Validation
Implementers run build/test jobs on Atlas under scripts/with-build-lock.sh. Capture an exact-source tagged artifact transfer and one real packaged-app smoke launch on the machine whose UI is being checked; use verified display, bounded timer and proven dismissal for computer use. Record remote failures as failures. No build or probe is being performed by this ticket-writing task.

## Dependencies
F1 is the foundation for F2 and F3. C11-215 (host build lock) is already done; reuse it. Retain C11-216 as the sole ticket for this scope.

## Risks
Current Xcode/signing readiness is unverified; refresh it. Avoid stale artifact provenance, simultaneous native builds, submodule cache mismatch and secrets in public logs. No UI strings expected; localize any introduced. Preserve operator availability on Hyperion.

Size: M. Tier: P0. Doctrine check: remote build infrastructure stays in project-owned paths; no tenant agent configuration edits or implicit production release.
title: Move c11 tagged builds, tests and release builds onto Atlas
